title: Two Arrested as Police Recover 11 Laptops, Three Phones in Maseno
desc: Two people are in custody after police recovered 11 laptops and three phones believed to have been stolen in Maseno Township, Kisumu County.
content:
Police in Maseno, Kisumu County, have arrested two people and recovered 11 laptops and three mobile phones believed to have been stolen from university students and other victims.

The National Police Service (NPS) said the operation followed a report made after a laptop was stolen from a hostel room on September 10, 2026. Investigators traced the device to an electronics repair shop in Maseno Township, where the complainant accompanied officers and identified it.

Police said the shop owner told them he had bought the laptop from another person. He subsequently contacted the seller and persuaded him to return to the shop, where officers arrested him.

A search of the seller led to the recovery of another laptop and a mobile phone. Police said the two devices were later confirmed to belong to a university student who had also reported a theft.

Investigators then searched the repair shop, recovering 10 additional laptops and two more mobile phones. According to the NPS, the shop owner could not account for the recovered devices or provide proof of ownership.

The two people are being held at Maseno Police Station pending arraignment. The recovered laptops and phones have been documented and retained as exhibits as investigations continue.

The police service has cautioned members of the public against buying electronic devices from unverified dealers or individuals who cannot provide legitimate proof of ownership.

The recovery also highlights the importance of checking the source of second-hand electronic devices before making purchases. Police said members of the public should report suspicious activities and suspected criminal activity to law enforcement.

The NPS has not said that all the recovered devices have been conclusively linked to particular theft cases. Investigations are continuing as officers establish the ownership and circumstances surrounding the other recovered items. 

The two people will face the next stage of the legal process once police complete their investigations and processing for arraignment.
